title: Watch with me (Matthew 26:36–56)
hookLine: he asks three friends to stay awake, then walks a little further, alone
tomorrow: two scenes, one house: a trial inside, and Peter in the courtyard…

lines: STAY ON THE PHONE WITH ME.
TARRY YE HERE, AND WATCH WITH ME.
THEN HE GOES A LITTLE FURTHER.
cards: People do this the night before surgery, or a funeral: stay on the phone, you don't have to say anything. Gethsemane has a strange version of it.
Jesus leaves most of the disciples at the edge: "Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder."

He takes Peter and the two sons of Zebedee further in and tells them, "My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me." Then he goes a little further, alone. Here's the puzzle.
Why ask friends to stay awake with you, and then walk away from them?

teach.h: LET THIS CUP PASS FROM ME.
teach.b: He falls on his face and prays: "O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt."

teach.h: COULD YE NOT WATCH ONE HOUR?
teach.b: He comes back, finds them asleep, and asks, "What, could ye not watch with me one hour?" There's the answer to the puzzle. He didn't need them to pray his prayer, or fix anything, or even understand it.
He needed them near, and awake. Watching is a way of being with someone in a place you can't follow them into.

teach.h: THE SPIRIT WILLING, THE FLESH WEAK.
teach.b: Then, before the scolding can land, he names what's happening in them: "the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak."
He prays a second time, and the prayer has moved: "thy will be done," a line from the prayer he taught them, now said in the dark. He finds them asleep again, and prays a third time.
Then a crowd with swords and staves, and Judas with a kiss.
Jesus says to him, "Friend, wherefore art thou come?" One disciple draws a sword, and Jesus stops it: "all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword."
And the scene ends: "Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled." What he'd asked for was so small.

how: Some churches keep a watch on the night of Maundy Thursday, before Good Friday, with people taking turns to pray, remembering Jesus' words: could ye not watch with me one hour?

games.q: two teammates promised to run with you at 6 a.m. before the big race. three mornings, they've slept through it. what does Gethsemane give you to say?
o: you meant it; the spirit is willing, the flesh is weak. try again tomorrow?
forget it. if you cared, you'd have been there. i'm done asking.
no problem at all, honestly. it doesn't matter to me.
games.why: Jesus names the failure (could ye not watch with me one hour?) and, in the same breath, the reason: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak. then he asks again.

practice: Before the sit begins, send one short message to someone having a hard time: thinking of you, or I'm here.

Then put the phone face down, and for the length of the sit, keep watch with them in your mind, awake, asking nothing of them. If no name comes to you, keep watch for whoever in your town is awake and afraid tonight.

wordCard.voice: Watch with me. Jesus' request to three friends in Gethsemane: not to fix his sorrow, only to stay awake beside it.

orig.note: Greek: watch, stay awake; Jesus' word to the disciples in Matthew 26:38.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: one hour, which is all he asked of them. Sleep well tonight.
